questions.q: In this pipeline, what partition key does the clickstream producer use, and why?
options: The user ID, so one user's session stays ordered on the same shard
A random UUID, so records spread evenly regardless of order
The event timestamp, so events sort chronologically across all shards
The page URL, so all traffic to one page lands on one shard
questions.explain: Using the user ID as the partition key guarantees every event from that user's session lands on the same shard, preserving order within the session.

questions.q: How does Firehose get the clickstream data in this pipeline?
options: It's configured to read directly from the Kinesis Data Stream as its source
A Lambda function polls the stream and calls Firehose's API for each record
Firehose has no way to read from a Kinesis Data Stream
The web application writes to Firehose and Kinesis Data Streams separately
questions.explain: Firehose can be configured with a Kinesis Data Stream as its source, pulling records continuously without a custom consumer application.

questions.q: What role does the Glue crawler play in this pipeline?
options: It discovers new S3 partitions written by Firehose and updates the Glue Data Catalog
It writes clickstream events directly into the Kinesis Data Stream
It replaces the need for Firehose entirely
It runs the windowed aggregation on the live stream
questions.explain: As in earlier chapters, the Glue crawler keeps the Data Catalog in sync with new partitions landing in S3, which is what makes the data queryable by Athena.

questions.q: What is Athena's role in this end-to-end pipeline?
options: Querying the clickstream data after it has landed and been cataloged in S3
Ingesting the raw clickstream events from the web application
Buffering records before they reach S3
Managing the Kinesis Data Stream's shard count
questions.explain: Athena handles the ad hoc, on-demand analysis step — querying data that Firehose already delivered and Glue already cataloged.

questions.q: Why use a Kinesis Data Stream in the middle of this pipeline instead of writing clickstream events straight to Firehose?
options: The stream provides durable, replayable, real-time ingestion that supports multiple independent consumers, which Firehose alone doesn't offer
Firehose cannot deliver data to S3 without a Kinesis Data Stream as a legal requirement
It has no real benefit and is purely optional overhead
A Kinesis Data Stream is required before Athena can query any data
questions.explain: The Data Stream adds real-time, replayable, multi-consumer capability (e.g., Kinesis Data Analytics could also read the same stream) that a direct-to-Firehose setup wouldn't provide.
